//: Machine-readable EVIDGATE_* configuration matrix (10.1.1-T1.1). One row per
variable: who consumes it, its type and boot constraints, whether it is a
secret, and — per environment — whether the environment must provide it and
where its value comes from.
scripts/check-env-matrix.mjs keeps this file honest: it discovers every key
from the options classes and key constants in src/, from .env.dev.template and
from infra/compose.dev.yml, and fails when a key is consumed but not declared,
declared but not consumed, or when a derivable field (consumers, type,
requiredAtBoot, constraints) disagrees with the source.
Origins: env-file = a committed dev template/.env.dev; environment = a plain
environment variable injected at deploy; secret-store = secret material
resolved at runtime and never written to the repo (10.1.1-T2/T3, O3 swap
point); repo-file = materialised by the dev stack from a committed infra file;
default = not provided, the option's own default applies.
required = required in that environment (the lint fails an environment that
does not declare it). requiredAtBoot = the process exits non-zero when it is
missing or malformed (01.1.2-T1's validated options). A row whose boot
requirement the parser cannot see names the enforcing site in requiredBy.
Provider-specific values are [OPEN] until 10.8.1 (O3) closes. See
docs/runbooks/environments.md.

keys.note: exactly the command-"evidgate_app" string, Host/Port/Database/Username/Password keys only: evidgate_app is the string `evidgate_app` and the boot refuses any other role name (00 §5.4.3); the password is generated per environment.

the custom-role write flag of 02.2.1-T2.2 (RECOMMENDATIONS 02-Q3): off in V1, where built-in roles are the only roles, so POST/PATCH /v1/roles answer 403 `forbidden`; on, the flagged commands may add a role to the caller's org (422 `unknown_permission` / `permission_not_assignable` still apply, and a built-in role stays immutable, 409). Nothing about an existing tenant is read differently while it is off, so no environment sets it.

base64 HS256 key (at least 32 bytes) that signs the `ci_producer` tokens minted by POST /v1/ci/token (02.4.1-T3.3, D7). Absent: the exchange answers 503 `unavailable` and no ci_producer bearer authenticates.
`iss` of the minted ci_producer token (02.4.1); default `evidgate`.
`aud` of the minted ci_producer token, which every ingest endpoint expects (02.4.1); default `evidgate`.
lifetime of a minted ci_producer token in minutes, at most 60 (02.4.1 AC6); default 60.
base64 current pepper (at least 32 bytes) behind the HMAC of ingest tokens and binding challenges (TL T5, DECISIONS D-A4). Absent: creating a binding or ingest token answers 503 `unavailable`.
version stored beside every HMAC made with the current pepper; bump it when the pepper rotates (02.4.2); default 1.
base64 previous pepper, kept while tokens made with it are still valid (rotation overlap, D-A4/D-A5).
version of the previous pepper; must differ from the current one; default 1.
expected `iss` of a GitHub Actions OIDC token (02.4.1-T1.1); default https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com.
expected `aud` of a GitHub Actions OIDC token, which the workflow requests (02.4.1); default `evidgate`.
JWKS document of the GitHub issuer; the boot refuses anything that is not https on the issuer's host (S4 allowlist, 02.4.1-T1.2).
clock skew tolerated on exp/nbf of a GitHub OIDC token (02.4.1-T4.2); default 60.
exchange attempts allowed per key (client address, repository id, token prefix) within the window (02.4.1 AC8); default 30.
comma-separated GitHub event_name values refused at the exchange (02.4.1 review); default pull_request_target, which runs in the base repository context while it may execute fork code.
length of the exchange rate-limit window in seconds (02.4.1 AC8); default 60.

`EVIDGATE:Login` (02.3.1-T1.1): absolute https base URL of the platform as a browser reaches it; the redirect URI registered at every provider is `{PublicBaseUrl}/v1/auth/oidc/{provider}/callback`, built from its origin, so a present value must be https with no path, query or fragment and `LoginOptionsValidator` fails the boot naming the key only (never the value). Absent is valid and starts no login: `GET /v1/auth/oidc/{provider}/start` and `/callback` answer 503 `unavailable` with `Retry-After` while every other route serves — no flag enables the routes. dev does not set it (the dev stack has no https origin); staging and prod inject their own origin as a plain variable at deploy.

`EVIDGATE:Login:StateLifetimeSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.1): lifetime in seconds of the pending-login cookie `__Host-evidgate_login` and of the one-time `state` it carries (02.3.1 §8: short-lived and one-time); default 600, accepted 60..900. No environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:Login:RetryAfterSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.1): value of the `Retry-After` header on the 503 `unavailable` a login route answers when its provider cannot be used (02.3.1 AC8), in seconds; default 30.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:ClientId` (02.3.1-T1.2): OAuth client id of the platform's own Google client; plain configuration, safe to log by name only and never a secret. Absent — or present without the client secret — leaves the provider unconfigured (`GoogleLoginProvider.IsConfigured`) and both Google routes answer 503 `unavailable` + `Retry-After`; there is no flag that enables login. dev sets neither credential (no https origin to complete a login on); staging and prod inject their own client id as a plain variable at deploy.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:ClientSecret` (02.3.1-T1.2): OAuth client secret of the Google login client, declared once in `SecretNames` (`OidcGoogleClientSecret`), resolved through `ISecretProvider` by `GoogleLoginOptionsSecretPostConfigure` — the property has an internal setter, so the binder never reads it from configuration — and never logged or put in an exception message. Absent with the client id, both Google routes answer 503 `unavailable` + `Retry-After` (no flag); staging and prod hold it in the provider secret store (10.1.1-T3), dev does not set it because the dev stack has no https origin to complete a login on.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:Issuer` (02.3.1-T1.2): expected `iss` of the Google ID token. The default `https://accounts.google.com` satisfies `[Required]`, so the key is not boot-required, and `GoogleLoginOptionsValidator` refuses any value other than it or its bare `accounts.google.com` alias — the issuer is not a per-environment preference, so no environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:AuthorizationEndpoint` (02.3.1-T1.2): browser-facing authorization endpoint, the target of the `start` redirect and never called by the server; default `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`. The validator refuses at boot a value that is not https on `accounts.google.com` with no userinfo and the default port (S4), so no environment overrides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:TokenEndpoint` (02.3.1-T1.2): token endpoint of the authorization-code exchange; default `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`. It must stay an https allowlisted Google host (`GoogleEndpoints.OutboundHosts`), checked at boot by the validator and again before every send by `GoogleOutboundAllowlistHandler` (S4), so no environment overrides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:JwksUri` (02.3.1-T1.2): document publishing the ID-token signing keys; default `https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs`. Same S4 allowlist and the same boot-time and per-send refusal as the token endpoint; no environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:ClockSkewSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.2): tolerance applied to `exp` and `nbf` of the ID token, in seconds; 02.3.1 AC2 fixes 60 and the option accepts 0..300, so the default is the policy and no environment overrides it.
`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:JwksTtlSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.2): how long a fetched JWKS document is trusted without a refresh attempt, in seconds; default 3600. No environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:JwksMinRefreshSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.2): the soonest an unknown `kid` in a presented ID token may force another JWKS fetch, in seconds; default 30, so a token stream naming random key ids cannot become one outbound call per request. No environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:HttpTimeoutSeconds` (02.3.1-T1.2): hard timeout of one outbound provider call, in seconds (P6); default 5. A call that times out is an outage, so the callback answers 503 rather than 401 (02.3.1 AC8). No environment provides it.

`EVIDGATE:OIDC:GOOGLE:MaxResponseBytes` (02.3.1-T1.2): largest provider response body the server reads, in bytes; default 65536, and a longer body is refused unread rather than buffered. No environment provides it.

boot-time RLS self-check switch (02.6.1-T1.4): Required (default) refuses to start unless every non-exempt table is under database-enforced isolation; Disabled exists only for hosts that boot without a database (contract/shutdown suites) and is logged at Warning on every boot. A deployable environment never sets Disabled — the config lint enforces that through forbiddenValues, not through this note.

absolute http(s) S3 endpoint of the object store (06.1.2-T1); empty selects the AWS regional endpoint of the region row. Dev points it at the local SeaweedFS gateway; staging and prod leave it unset until 10.1.1-T3 provisions the bucket. The options validator accepts only an absolute http(s) URL with no userinfo, query or fragment, so a crafted value cannot redirect the signed request at another host (SSRF-by-config).

SigV4 signing region of the object store (06.1.2-T1). Dev uses the SeaweedFS gateway's us-east-1; staging and prod set the provider region, which is [OPEN] until 10.8.1 (O3) and is a residency criterion for plan 11.

bucket the pending/ staging keys live in (06.1.2-T1). Dev uses the same bucket scripts/dev/up.sh creates and puts the pending/ 24 h lifecycle rule on; staging and prod get their own bucket with versioning and lifecycle from 10.1.1-T3 and 10.5.1-T2.

lifetime of a presigned PUT in seconds (06.1.2-T1, 00 §9.3: at most 15 minutes); option default 900, and the options validator accepts 1..900 only. No environment sets it: the default is the contract.

path-style S3 addressing (06.1.2-T1); option default true, which every S3-compatible emulator needs. Dev states it explicitly because SeaweedFS requires it; a real provider accepts virtual-host style, so staging and prod keep the default.

access key of the object-storage identity (06.1.2-T1), resolved through ISecretProvider by the options post-configurer and never bound from IConfiguration. Dev uses the local-only SeaweedFS identity that scripts/dev/up.sh asserts equals infra/seaweedfs/s3-config.json; staging and prod hold their own credential in the provider secret store (10.1.1-T3).

secret key of the object-storage identity (06.1.2-T1), resolved through ISecretProvider by the options post-configurer and never bound from IConfiguration. Dev uses the local-only SeaweedFS identity that scripts/dev/up.sh asserts equals infra/seaweedfs/s3-config.json; staging and prod hold their own credential in the provider secret store (10.1.1-T3).

expanded-size cap of an event batch (04.1.1-T3.2, DECISIONS §8.1 D-A8): the byte count a `Content-Encoding: gzip` body may expand to on `POST /v1/runs/{r}/events`, measured while decoding and before any parse or write. Exceeding it — or the ratio cap of EVIDGATE__INGESTION__MAXEXPANSIONRATIO — is 413 `batch_too_large` with no write; the raw 1 MiB transport cap and the 500-event cap stay code constants (contract numbers, not options). Option default 8388608 (8 MiB); the range 1048576..67108864 stops a deployment from disabling the cap or setting it below one legal 1 MiB batch.

expanded/compressed ratio cap of a gzip event batch (04.1.1-T3.2, DECISIONS §8.1 D-A8): decoding refuses once expanded bytes / compressed bytes read exceeds this value, so a small body cannot expand without bound (the 50 MiB-from-20 KiB bomb). Paired with EVIDGATE__INGESTION__MAXEXPANDEDBYTES; either overrun is 413 `batch_too_large` with no write. Option default 20 (20:1); the range 1..1000 keeps the guard meaningful.

collection deadline offset applied at run create when no policy revision is pinned (05.2.1 AC12, T93): run.collection_deadline_at = created_at + this value, computed on the database clock. A TimeSpan literal (02:00:00 = 2 h, the default; ⚠️ tuned ≈ p95 × 1.5). 07.1.1-T4 replaces it with the pinned policy's collection_timeout once the run-pinning handshake lands. Bounded at boot to more than 00:00:00 and at most 366 days (the scale of the 525600-minute late-window cap) by RunsOptions.CollectionTimeoutAttribute: a non-positive value would place collection_deadline_at at or before created_at on the immutable column, and an extreme value would overflow the interval arithmetic. No constraints block: the lint derives constraints from C# attributes, and no DataAnnotations range carries a TimeSpan.

late-window snapshot written at run create when no policy revision is pinned (05.2.1 AC12, T93/T62): run.late_window_minutes, immutable after create. Default 1440 (24 h). 07.1.1-T4 copies the pinned policy's late window instead.
task-queue retry backoff base, `base × 2^attempts` (01.5.1-T1.3); default 5.
retry backoff ceiling; must be ≥ BACKOFFBASESECONDS (a relative rule the options Validate enforces); default 3600.
rows one claim pass takes per queue; default 50.
concurrent claim loops for a queue only a schedule declares; default 1.
undispatched outbox rows one dispatch batch moves (01.5.1-T3.1); default 200.
queue an outbox-dispatched task lands in when QUEUEROUTES has no entry; default "default".
milliseconds the outbox dispatcher waits between passes; default 1000.
milliseconds one consumer loop waits between claim passes; default 1000.
indexed queue of QUEUEROUTES entry <n>; empty list by default.
indexed task_type of QUEUEROUTES entry <n>, unique across entries; empty list by default.
concurrent claim loops for QUEUES entry <n>; empty list by default.
non-empty queue name of QUEUES entry <n> (≤ 64 chars); empty list by default.
how far back the schedule runner looks for due occurrences — wider than the poll interval on purpose, so a missed tick is late, not lost (01.5.1-T1.4); default 300.
milliseconds between schedule-runner passes; default 60000.

command-"evidgate_worker_sched" string — the only role with EXECUTE on the owner SECURITY DEFINER sweeps (TL T80, e.g. the scheduled idempotency purge). Optional at boot: a Worker without it still consumes ordinary tasks and the sweep task fails loudly naming this key.
task lease length (`locked_until = now() + this`); must exceed the longest handler because a handler that outlives its lease can run twice (at-least-once, A10); default 300.

absolute http(s) OTLP/gRPC endpoint of the collector (10.3.1-T2). Unset disables the exporter, so dev omits it; staging and prod must set it (FR-10-5, 00 §11). Backend, region and exact endpoint are [OPEN] until 10.3.1-T2 settles them.

IP address the Worker's minimal /internal/health/* listener binds; the default is 0.0.0.0, which is what a container probe needs, so a deployment that wants a different address states it explicitly. Dev sets 127.0.0.1 (00 §5.7, §9.1: the operational path must not be reachable off-host) and the smoke test asserts the bind address. A malformed value fails the boot ([Required] plus the IP-literal validator); a missing one does not, because the default already satisfies the attribute — which is why requiredAtBoot is false while dev still declares it (a security-relevant value stays visible per environment).
TCP port of the Worker's minimal /internal/health/* listener; default 8081, and infra/<env>/environment.json probes.worker.baseUrl must point at the same port when a value is set.
milliseconds between readiness polls while the consumer waits for the database; default 1000.

dev-stack only: password of the evidgate_app role, generated by scripts/dev/up.sh from the __EVIDGATE_APP_PASSWORD__ placeholder; it is what makes EVIDGATE__DATABASE__CONNECTIONSTRING concrete in dev. Staging/prod get the same role's password from the provider secret store instead.
dev-stack only: loopback port the compose PostgreSQL 18 publishes; the dev connection strings embed the same port (scripts/dev/up.sh does not rewrite them).
dev-stack only: password of the compose superuser, used by scripts/dev/db-init.sh for the bootstrap (roles + database) and never by Api, Worker or Migrator (00 §5.4.3).
statement timeout of the migration job; 0 (default) means no timeout, because a long index build must not be cut in half — the deploy gate bounds the run instead (10.2.2).

command-"evidgate_owner" string — the only writer of public.schema_migration and of DDL (01.4.1). MigratorOptions.FromEnvironment throws MigratorSetupException naming the variable, so a missing value exits non-zero before any connection is opened.

directory holding migrations/; unset resolves <checkout>/migrations by walking up to Evidgate.slnx and falls back to the application directory. ⚠️ what the Evidgate.Migrator image ships is settled in 10.2.1-T1.
dev-stack only: password of the audited read-only evidgate_operator role (01.4.1-T2); consumed by the operator runbooks, not by the hosts.
dev-stack only: password of the evidgate_owner migration role, generated by scripts/dev/up.sh; it is what makes EVIDGATE_MIGRATOR__CONNECTIONSTRING concrete in dev.

dev-stack only: local SeaweedFS identity access key; committed on purpose in infra/seaweedfs/s3-config.json and asserted equal by scripts/dev/up.sh, because it is accepted only by the local container (01.8.1-T1).

dev-stack only: bucket scripts/dev/up.sh creates and carries the pending/ 24 h lifecycle rule (T18). The runtime object-storage options arrive with 06.3.1; staging/prod bucket names land with 10.1.1-T3.
dev-stack only: absolute S3 endpoint of the local SeaweedFS gateway.
dev-stack only: loopback port the compose SeaweedFS gateway publishes and the port embedded in EVIDGATE_S3_ENDPOINT.
dev-stack only: SigV4 region the dev bucket requests are signed with (us-east-1 locally; the provider region is [OPEN] until O3)
dev-stack only: local SeaweedFS identity secret key, same committed local-only identity as EVIDGATE_S3_ACCESS_KEY.

dev-stack only: the whole SeaweedFS identity file, exported by scripts/dev/up.sh from infra/seaweedfs/s3-config.json and written inside the container (a host bind mount is unusable under colima/virtiofs; infra/README.md records the evidence). Secret because it carries the access/secret key pair.

dev-stack only: password of the evidgate_worker_sched role, the only role with EXECUTE on the owner SECURITY DEFINER sweeps (TL T80); it is what makes EVIDGATE__TASKS__SWEEPCONNECTIONSTRING concrete in dev.
